seen_animation: A line-drawn wine glass (rounded bowl, flat ellipse rim, double-line stem) stands inside a grey rectangular box with a small post at the right and horizontal grey lines on both sides. A straight black straw sits in the bowl. Across the 16 frames the straw rocks: it leans right in frames 1-3, stands upright in frame 4, leans right again in 5-7, is upright in 8, leans right in 9-10, tips slightly left in 11, leans right in 12, is upright to left-leaning in 13-15, and in frame 16 swings to a steep diagonal leaning right. The whole glass and box drift slightly left and right and up and down between frames, as if the camera is handheld.
seen_film: A real wine glass with a white straw in it stands inside a clear acrylic box with a metal post on the right, in front of a pink-red bench. The straw rattles inside the vibrating glass, switching between a right lean, upright and a left lean: right in 1-3, upright in 4, right in 5-7, near upright in 8, right in 9-10, left in 11, right in 12, upright to left in 13-15, and in 16 a blurred steep diagonal as the straw is thrown hard. The camera framing drifts slightly side to side.
named_subject: A wine glass with a straw in it, vibrating inside a box (resonance demonstration)
evidence: a.png/d.png: the straw angle matches the film at all 16 sample frames (right lean 1-3, upright 4, right 5-7, upright 8, left 11, upright/left 13-15, steep diagonal 16 in both). e.png vs f.png: upright straw at 6-7 and 11-15 in both; right lean at 8 and 19 in both; left lean at 17-18 and 23 in both; steep diagonal at 26 matching the blurred diagonal in film frame 26. Box, post and bench lines sit at the same places in the frame as the film's box, post and bench. The side-to-side drift of the glass in g.png matches the camera drift visible in f.png. The straw changes angle sharply between 22, 23, 24 and 26, but the film's straw flips in the same frames, so these read as the event and not as pops. Judged from still frames only, not playback.
primary_gap: The bowl outline changes width and lean slightly from frame to frame (for example 8 to 9 and 25 to 26), more than the film's glass does, so the glass body may shimmer in playback.
closes_when: The bowl outline keeps the same width and shape across consecutive frames and only shifts position with the camera drift, while the straw alone changes angle.
protect: The straw angle timing matching the film frame for frame; the doodle's construction (oval rim, tapered bowl, double-line stem, single-line straw); the sparse grey box/post/bench scenery placed where the film's objects are; the camera drift that follows the film.
identity_gap: The glass keeps the doodle's oval rim, tapered bowl and double-line stem with the same loose single stroke; the doodle's base is out of frame, as in the film's crop.
